interfaces: JSON envelope { schemaVersion, ok, command, data, error }
Implemented commands help, version, next, status, explain task/transition/validation/reviews/merge, start, validate, manual export/import/run; command-owned contracts documented in docs/CLI.md

behavioralConstraints: JSON mode emits exactly one top-level envelope object for normal success or expected command failure
documented npm machine invocation suppresses npm lifecycle logging so stdout remains exactly one CLI envelope
next returns selected empty complete or blocked as command-specific data while preserving the top-level envelope
invalid task or dependency repository input that prevents trustworthy selection fails rather than returning partial success
expected workflow blockers use the existing exit 4 contract; observational blocked/empty next or status results remain exit 0
status emits the same ProjectStatus model as human text or JSON data with statusVersion 1.0.0 and LOCAL_REGISTERED_TASKS scope; top-level envelope version remains 1.0.0
default next reads the same validated persisted lifecycle map as status while preserving explicit taskStates injection and unchanged BOOT-008 selection policy
status invalid or changing input fails closed with exit 70 rather than partial successful data
explain emits one WorkflowExplanation with diagnosticsVersion 1.0.0 and explicit scope in the unchanged schemaVersion 1.0.0 envelope

explain observed missing failed stale blocked findings are successful exit 0 data; invalid arguments task identity or transition transport/role policy use exit 2, invalid/changing authoritative input uses exit 70
explain clear means no observed failure in its declared scope and never gate approval; task transition validation review and merge producers retain policy authority

explain merge optionally uses existing authorized GITHUB_REPOSITORY and GITHUB_TOKEN/GH_TOKEN read configuration; absent configuration produces an explicit blocked finding without authentication or secret display
invariants: identical argv, observation timestamp, and equivalent repository/task-state inputs produce deterministic normal command results
shell behavior does not require an AI provider
registration of a reserved command never implies implemented workflow semantics
BOOT-008 next routing performs no assignment lifecycle mutation branch mutation review or merge behavior
status performs no state mutation, fetch, assignment acquisition/recovery, gate approval, provider invocation, or merge
explain performs no state initialization or workflow mutation, validator/review execution, agent invocation, Git fetch, recovery, PR write, or merge
examples: npm run --silent agent -- --json version emits only a success envelope on stdout and exits 0
npm run --silent agent -- --json next emits BOOT-008 selection data and exits 0 when evaluated successfully
review exits 3 with COMMAND_NOT_IMPLEMENTED while generic review CLI wiring remains reserved
npm run --silent agent -- --json status emits one local registered-task status aggregate in data
edgeCases: --json may appear before or after the command token
empty valid task registry makes next return a successful empty result
empty valid task registry makes status return kind empty and zero counts, never synthetic GitHub bootstrap progress

expectations: stable top-level envelope and documented exit-code meanings
registered reserved commands do not report success without implemented behavior
command-specific data can evolve additively without changing top-level envelope meanings
requiredReachableRanges: successful next data containing selected task ID and canonical branch
successful status data with explicit local scope and empty blocked stale or unknown facts preserved
successful explain data with all five scopes and missing failed stale blocked conditions, without treating clear as gate approval
